title: Ananias and Sapphira (Acts 5:1–11)
hook: a hard story about pretending to give more than they gave
tomorrow: the council wants them dead. one teacher stands up. what does he say?

segments.voice: Yesterday Barnabas sold a field and laid the money at the apostles' feet: be a Barnabas. Today another couple makes the same move.

A filter can make a plate of food look bigger than it is. Ananias and his wife Sapphira sell land, like Barnabas did, and bring money to the apostles' feet. But they keep back part of the price and let it look like everything. Why does their story end so hard? Not because they kept some. Because they pretended. A gentle heads-up, for anyone listening with kids: this is a hard story, and two people die in it.
screen: `A FILTER ON THE PLATE.` → `PART OF THE PRICE, KEPT BACK.` → `A HARD STORY, GENTLY.`

segments.voice: Watch the hands first. The same gesture as yesterday: money laid at the apostles' feet. Same hands, same feet, same move. One is a gift; the other is a performance. Peter sees through it: "Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land?" Then two questions that change how the whole story reads: "Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power?" The land was theirs. The money was theirs. Keeping some was never the problem. "Thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God." And "Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost." Some hours later Sapphira comes in, not knowing. Peter gives her a chance to tell it straight: "Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much? And she said, Yea, for so much." Then a sound: footsteps. The young men who buried her husband are at the door, and she falls too. Acts ends the scene with "great fear came upon all the church." Readers take this story different ways: as God's judgment, as a warning to a young community held together by trust, as a sign of how seriously Acts takes honesty. Acts doesn't explain itself. One to tell a friend tonight: in this story, keeping money was allowed. Pretending was not.
screen: `SAME HANDS, SAME FEET.` · `WAS IT NOT THINE OWN?` · `NOT UNTO MEN, BUT UNTO GOD.` · `FOOTSTEPS AT THE DOOR.` · then, large: `NO PRETENDING.`

segments.voice: Rest your hands on your knees, palms up and empty. Let them be the plain truth about what you give, your time, your money, your effort, no more and no less than it is. Breathe with open hands and nothing hidden in them.
Ananias and Sapphira. A couple who kept back part of the price and pretended it was all: Acts' hard story about honesty.
Hold onto this: no pretending; give what you give, and call it what it is. Day nine of Acts.

notes: A hard story (two deaths): the hook gives parents one gentle heads-up line; the deaths are given in the text's own words (5:5) and briefly (5:10), with no drama. The three readings (judgment, a warning to a young community, how seriously Acts takes honesty) are named without ranking. Confirm.
'Some hours later' softens Acts 5:7's 'about the space of three hours after' (no number stated in the voice).
'Footsteps… the young men who buried her husband are at the door' paraphrases Acts 5:6, 9–10.
Trapdoor: νοσφίζομαι (5:2, 'kept back') and the Septuagint of Joshua 7:1 (Achan); a scholar should confirm before this floor is used.
